notes:
Piston numbering now follows the last piston you placed.

**Place a piston and the next one carries on from it**, rather than from the highest number in the piece. The two only differ when you work backwards or correct a number: renumbering a piston from 320 down to 250 used to leave the next placement at 321, and now gives you 251 — which is where the console actually is. On a freshly opened piece it still starts from the highest number present, because nothing records the order pistons were placed in.

Also in this build, since 1.87:

**The organ belongs to an ink layer.** Pick an organ while editing a piston and it now applies to that ink layer of that piece only, instead of changing every piston in every piece. Each piston keeps its registrations for every organ it has been used on, so switching away and back loses nothing, and the organ list shows how many pistons in the piece have stops saved on each one.

**A metronome**, on both the page and the sidebar. Place a button with its own tempo, choose whether it ticks, and optionally have it stop itself after a set number of seconds. Long-press the metronome tool to start one without placing a button; a Stop button appears in the top corner while it runs. It keeps going through page turns and stops when you open another piece. Volume is the tablet's own.

**Arrow keys for turning pages in edit mode**, at the right end of the tab bar, and a choice in reader settings between tapping the edges and swiping to turn.

**Hovering the pen no longer opens edit mode** unless you actually write something.

Several fixes worth knowing: a Back button placed on the second tablet no longer reverts to a page link; copying an ink layer now reaches the other tablet; a hidden page dims straight away in page management; ink no longer vanishes for two or three seconds when the sidebar appears after writing; and the tablets exchange far less housekeeping traffic when a piece opens.

Your library, annotations and licence are not affected.
